subject: Decision Making
subcategory: The Science of Risk and Reward
title: Availability Heuristic

hook.text: After a plane crash, flight bookings drop for weeks. After a shark attack, beaches empty.

buildup.text: Tversky and Kahneman showed we estimate frequency by how easily examples come to mind. Vivid events feel common.

discovery.text: Media amplifies this. News covers plane crashes, not car accidents.

twist.text: The availability heuristic also affects experts. Doctors overdiagnose conditions they recently encountered in other.

climax.text: Ease of recall is not frequency. What we remember most vividly is often what matters least statistically.

punchline.text: Easy to remember, easy to overestimate. Memory distorts our sense of risk.

quiz.question: What does the availability heuristic cause us to do?
options: Overestimate the frequency of events that are vivid and easy to recall
